items.new: "On the eastern shore of our Lake Erie, Don; but — I beg your patience — perhaps you shall soon hear more of all that. Now, gentlemen, in square-sail brigs and three-masted ships, nearly as large and sturdy as any that ever sailed out of your old Callao to far Manilla, this Lakeman, in the landlocked heart of our America, had nonetheless been raised on all those agrarian, freebooting impressions popularly connected with the open ocean. For taken all together, those grand freshwater seas of ours — Erie, and Ontario, and Huron, and Superior, and Michigan — have an ocean-like expanse, with many of the ocean's noblest traits, and with many of its varieties of races and climates around their rims. They contain round archipelagoes of romantic islands, just as the Polynesian waters do; for much of their length they are bordered by two great contrasting nations, as the Atlantic is; they provide long sea approaches to our many territorial colonies from the East, dotted all around their banks; here and there they are frowned upon by batteries, and by the goat-like, craggy guns of lofty Mackinaw; they have heard the swift thunder of naval victories; at intervals they yield their beaches to wild barbarians, whose red-painted faces flash out from their fur-hide wigwams; for leagues and leagues they are flanked by ancient, untrodden forests, where the gaunt pines stand like serried lines of kings in Gothic family trees, those same woods sheltering wild African beasts of prey, and silky-coated creatures whose exported furs make robes for Tartar Emperors; they mirror the paved capitals of Buffalo and Cleveland, as well as Winnebago villages; they float alike the full-rigged merchant ship, the armed cruiser of the State, the steamer, and the beech canoe; they are swept by north winds and dismasting blasts as terrible as any that lash the salt sea; they know what shipwrecks are, for out of sight of land, however inland, they have drowned many a ship at midnight with all its shrieking crew. So, gentlemen, though an inlander, Steelkilt was born to the wild ocean and raised on the wild ocean — as bold a mariner as any. And as for Radney: though as an infant he may have lain down on the lonely Nantucket beach to nurse at his mother the sea; though in later life he had long followed our austere Atlantic and your contemplative Pacific — he was still quite as vengeful and quarrelsome as the backwoods seaman fresh from the latitudes of buckhorn-handled Bowie knives. Yet this Nantucketer was a man with some good-hearted traits; and this Lakeman was a mariner who, though a sort of devil indeed, could still be handled by unbending firmness, tempered only by that common decency of human recognition which is the right of the lowliest slave; treated that way, this Steelkilt had long been kept harmless and docile. At any rate, he had proved so up to then; but Radney was doomed and driven mad, and Steelkilt — but, gentlemen, you shall hear."

items.new: "For three hundred and sixty miles, gentlemen, through the entire breadth of the state of New York; through numerous populous cities and most thriving villages; through long, dismal, uninhabited swamps, and rich cultivated fields unrivaled for fertility; by billiard-room and bar-room; through the holy of holies of great forests; on Roman arches over Indian rivers; through sun and shade; by happy hearts or broken; through all the wide, contrasting scenery of those noble Mohawk counties; and especially by rows of snow-white chapels, whose spires stand almost like milestones — there flows one continuous stream of life as corrupt as Venice's and often lawless. There's your true Ashantee, gentlemen; there your pagans howl; where you always find them, next door to you, under the long-cast shadow and the snug, patronizing shelter of churches. For by some curious fatality, just as it is often noted that your big-city robbers always camp around the halls of justice, so sinners, gentlemen, most abound in the holiest neighborhoods."

items.new: "Freely portrayed in his own calling, gentlemen, the Canaller would make a fine dramatic hero, so abundantly and picturesquely wicked is he. Like Mark Antony, for days and days along his green-turfed, flowery Nile, he lazily floats, openly toying with his red-cheeked Cleopatra, ripening his apricot thigh on the sunny deck. But ashore, all this softness is dashed away. The brigand-like getup the Canaller so proudly sports, and his slouched and gaily ribboned hat, proclaim his grand features. A terror to the smiling innocence of the villages he floats through, his swarthy face and bold swagger are shunned in the cities too. Once, when I was a vagabond on his own canal, I received good turns from one of these Canallers; I thank him heartily, and would not wish to be ungrateful; but it is often one of the chief redeeming qualities of your man of violence that at times he has as stiff an arm to back a poor stranger in a tight spot as to rob a wealthy one. In sum, gentlemen, how wild this canal life is, is emphatically shown by this: that our wild whale-fishery contains so many of its most finished graduates, and that hardly any breed of men, except Sydney men, are so much distrusted by our whaling captains. Nor does it at all lessen the curiousness of this matter that, for many thousands of our country boys and young men born along its route, the probationary life of the Grand Canal furnishes the only transition between quietly reaping in a Christian cornfield and recklessly plowing the waters of the most barbaric seas."

items.new: "I left off, gentlemen, where the Lakeman shook the backstay. Hardly had he done so when he was surrounded by the three junior mates and the four harpooners, who all crowded him to the deck. But sliding down the ropes like baleful comets, the two Canallers rushed into the uproar and tried to drag their man out of it toward the forecastle. Others of the sailors joined them in this attempt, and a tangled melee followed; while, standing well out of harm's way, the valiant captain danced up and down with a whale-pike, calling on his officers to manhandle that atrocious scoundrel and smoke him out and along to the quarter-deck. Now and then he ran close up to the whirling edge of the confusion, and, prying into the heart of it with his pike, tried to prick out the object of his resentment. But Steelkilt and his desperadoes were too much for them all; they succeeded in reaching the forecastle deck, where, hastily swinging three or four large casks around into a line with the windlass, these sea-Parisians entrenched themselves behind the barricade."

items.new: "No need, gentlemen; one moment, and I'll go on. — Now, gentlemen, suddenly seeing the snowy whale within fifty yards of the ship — forgetting the pact among the crew — in the excitement of the moment the Teneriffe man had instinctively and involuntarily raised his voice for the monster, though for some little time past it had been plainly visible from the three sullen mastheads. Everything was now a frenzy. 'The White Whale — the White Whale!' was the cry from captain, mates, and harpooners, who, undeterred by fearful rumors, were all eager to capture so famous and precious a fish; while the sullen crew eyed sideways, and with curses, the appalling beauty of the vast milky mass that, lit up by the level, spangling rays of the sun, shifted and glistened like a living opal in the blue morning sea. Gentlemen, a strange fatality runs through the whole course of these events, as if truly mapped out before the world itself was charted. The mutineer was the mate's bowsman, and when they were fast to a whale, it was his duty to sit next to him, while Radney stood up with his lance in the bow, and to haul in or slacken the line at the word of command. Moreover, when the four boats were lowered, the mate's got the start; and no one howled more fiercely with delight than Steelkilt as he strained at his oar. After a hard pull, their harpooner got fast, and, spear in hand, Radney sprang to the bow. He was always a furious man in a boat, it seems. And now his bandaged cry was to beach him on the whale's topmost back. Only too willing, his bowsman hauled him up and up, through a blinding foam that blended two whitenesses together, until suddenly the boat struck as if against a sunken ledge, and, tipping over, spilled out the standing mate. At that instant, as he fell on the whale's slippery back, the boat righted and was dashed aside by the swell, while Radney was tossed over into the sea on the other flank of the whale. He struck out through the spray, and for an instant was dimly seen through that veil, wildly trying to get himself out of the eye of Moby Dick. But the whale rushed around in a sudden maelstrom, seized the swimmer between his jaws, and, rearing high up with him, plunged headlong again and went down."
